- File: workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: `_git_invocation_targets`, lines 1065-1068 (the `if unjudgeable:` early return) sits INSIDE the `if repo_dir is None:` block (lines 1052-1069).
  Problem: The CDPATH-redirectable `cd` block only sets `unjudgeable_reason` on the returned `GuardTarget` while `repo_dir is None`. Once a later segment resets the directory (a `;` or `&` separator in `guard_targets` rewrites `directory = session_cwd` at lines 1148-1153) and a follow-up `cd ./sub` re-resolves it, `repo_dir` is the resolved session-cwd-relative path. `_git_invocation_targets` then falls through the `if repo_dir is None:` block (and therefore the `if unjudgeable:` check) into either the `if subcommand == "commit":` branch (line 1071, returns `GuardTarget(subcommand, repo_dir, "", "HEAD", False)` with no `unjudgeable_reason`) or the `return _push_refspec_targets(...)` call at line 1073 (which has no `unjudgeable` parameter at all). `_evaluate_bash` (line 1973-1977) only blocks when `target.unjudgeable_reason` is set, so neither the commit nor the push is blocked.
  Why it fails at runtime: `CDPATH=<parent> cd .git; git push origin HEAD:feature/x` (and the same with `git commit -m x`) reaches the `;` separator, `directory` is reset to `session_cwd`, the unjudgeable flag stays set from segment 1 (the comment at line 1136 says "Once set, neither is cleared"), but `_git_invocation_targets` returns a target without `unjudgeable_reason`. Bash pushed from the CDPATH-redirected worktree while the guard judged `session_cwd` — exactly the wrong-repository path the §21 fix was supposed to close. The same exploit works with `cd ./sub` between the CDPATH cd and the guarded call: `CDPATH=<parent> cd .git; cd ./sub && git push origin HEAD:feature/x` (or `git commit -m x`). The fixture `_cdpath_exploit_layout` in the test file already builds the `CDPATH=<parent> cd wt` shape that triggers this; the corresponding `;`-reset path is missing from the parametrize list.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: same as above — the structural placement of `if unjudgeable:` inside `if repo_dir is None:`.
  Problem: The unjudgeable rule is meant to mark any later guarded call as "Bash may have entered a different repo, refuse to judge". The current placement conditions it on the directory being still-unknown, so any resolved directory downstream of a CDPATH `cd` re-enables the (now-incorrect) session-checkout fallback for push and the same unjudgeable-less `GuardTarget` for commit.
  Why it fails at runtime: As above — push and commit both bypass when a `;` / `&` reset + `cd ./sub` gives the call a real-looking `cwd`. The same shape with `&&` (no reset, `repo_dir` stays `None`) does get blocked by the inner `if unjudgeable:` branch, which is why the current tests pass — every parameterization keeps `repo_dir is None` at the guarded call.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py
  Line or code reference: `test_a_cd_that_cdpath_may_redirect_makes_later_calls_unjudgeable` parametrize list (the CDPATH case block in the diff) and the e2e tests under it.
  Problem: None of the parametrize cases or e2e tests use a `;` (or `&`) separator between the CDPATH cd and the guarded call to drive a directory reset. The list mixes inline-prefix, `set or used earlier`, push and commit, `builtin --` and `command -p --`, `+=`, and the worktree exploit, but the only separator before the guarded call is `&&` (no reset) — so every test case leaves `repo_dir is None` at the guarded call and the inner `if unjudgeable:` branch fires. The bypass shape (`cd wt; cd ./sub && git push` or `cd wt; git commit -m x`) is therefore not covered, and the e2e `_cdpath_exploit_layout` helper already builds the exact fixture (a `wt` directory in the clean repo next to the stranded worktree) needed to add the missing case — the e2e test just needs `cd ./wt` (or no second cd at all) after the `;` separator.
  Why it fails at runtime: Without a test that resets the directory between the CDPATH cd and the guarded call, the bug above ships green and the §21 CDPATH fix leaves a one-token bypass. The e2e test only runs the inline / bare / export / builtin / append forms, all of which use `cd wt` as the final cd.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

AD-5 explicitly says commit is in scope, but the only `if unjudgeable:` branch is the one inside `if repo_dir is None:`; there is no `if unjudgeable:` in the `if subcommand == "commit":` branch and no `unjudgeable` parameter to `_push_refspec_targets`.
